questions.stem: What does Data Product Ownership refer to?
options: The responsibility of managing and overseeing a data product from creation through to ongoing improvements
The legal ownership of the servers on which data is stored
The copyright held over a published dataset
The task of writing SQL queries for a dashboard
The right to sell data to third parties
questions.explanation: Data Product Ownership is the responsibility of managing and overseeing a data product from its creation through to its ongoing improvement.

questions.stem: When defining vision and goals for a sales dashboard, what would a Data Product Owner decide?
options: Which programming language the engineers must use
What metrics and insights will help users make informed sales decisions
How much the sales team is paid
Which cloud provider to buy servers from
When the sales team should take their breaks
questions.explanation: For a sales dashboard, the DPO defines which metrics and insights will help users make informed sales decisions.

questions.stem: How does a Data Product Owner decide which features or improvements to develop first?
options: By building every feature at the same time
By choosing the features that are cheapest regardless of value
By prioritising based on their value to users and the organisation, balancing short-term needs with long-term goals
By following the order in which requests were received
By letting the engineers pick their favourite features
questions.explanation: The DPO prioritises features by their value to users and the organisation, balancing short-term needs with long-term goals in a roadmap.

questions.stem: What does 'Understand User Needs' involve for a Data Product Owner?
options: Guessing what users want without asking them
Reading only the technical documentation
Restricting the product to expert users
Gathering feedback, studying user behaviour and ensuring the product addresses actual problems
Hiring more data engineers
questions.explanation: The DPO connects with end users, gathers feedback and studies user behaviour so the product addresses actual problems or enhances the user experience.

questions.stem: With whom does a Data Product Owner collaborate to ensure data quality and compliance?
options: External auditors only
The marketing department
Customers and suppliers
The board of directors
Data engineers and analysts
questions.explanation: The DPO collaborates with data engineers and analysts to ensure the data product meets high standards and complies with privacy regulations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a key responsibility of Data Product Ownership?
options: Negotiating the company's office lease
Defining vision and goals
Prioritising features and improvements
Ensuring data quality and compliance
Monitoring product performance
questions.explanation: The listed responsibilities cover vision, prioritisation, user needs, quality and compliance, cross-functional collaboration and performance monitoring; office leases are not among them.

questions.stem: What does a Data Product Owner monitor after a data product is launched?
options: The salaries of the development team
Key performance indicators (KPIs) to assess how well the product meets its goals and user needs
The weather forecast for the region
Only the number of servers in use
The stock price of competitors
questions.explanation: After launch, the DPO monitors KPIs to assess how well the product meets its goals, informing decisions to update features, fix issues or adjust direction.

questions.stem: Which cross-functional team members does a Data Product Owner work with to bring a data product to life?
options: Only data scientists
Only business leaders
Data scientists, engineers, designers and business leaders
Only external consultants
Only the finance department
questions.explanation: The DPO works closely with data scientists, engineers, designers and business leaders so the technical foundation is solid and the product serves business purposes.

questions.stem: Why does Data Product Ownership matter?
options: It removes the need for data engineers
It guarantees that a data product never needs to change
It allows data products to be sold to competitors
It bridges the gap between technical data capabilities and business needs
It replaces data governance entirely
questions.explanation: Data product ownership is crucial because it bridges the gap between technical data capabilities and business needs, keeping products maintained and refined.

questions.stem: What is the bottom line on Data Product Ownership?
options: It is a temporary role that ends once the product is launched
It concerns only the initial design of a data product
It applies only to dashboards, not to datasets or models
It is mainly about cost control
It is about taking end-to-end responsibility for a data product, from its initial idea to its continuous improvement
questions.explanation: Data product ownership means end-to-end responsibility for a data product, from the initial idea through continuous improvement.
